subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the absolute extremum of f(x) = x² defined on [−2, 2].

mark_split.label: Evaluate f at the critical point and at both endpoints
Compare the values and state both extrema

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say which points you must test on a closed interval, and say how many places the maximum value is reached at here.

steps.label: Find the critical point
steps.margin_note: First mark. State that f is continuous on the closed interval — that is what guarantees the absolute maximum and minimum exist. Then check the critical point actually lies inside the interval.
lines: f(x) = x² on the closed interval [−2, 2].
f is continuous on [−2, 2] and differentiable on (−2, 2), so an absolute maximum and an absolute minimum both exist on this interval.
x = 0 lies inside [−2, 2], so it is a critical point to be tested.

recall.must_convey: That f′(x) = 2x is zero only at x = 0, which lies inside [−2, 2].
accept: differentiate x squared to get two x
two x equals zero gives x equal to zero
the only critical point is at the origin
derivative zero pettina x zero vasthundi
zero lies inside the interval so it must be tested
f is continuous on the closed interval

steps.why: An absolute extremum on a closed interval sits either where the derivative is zero or at an endpoint. Differentiating finds the first group, and there is only one such point here.
common_mistakes: Reporting x = ±2 as critical points, when they are endpoints rather than points where f′ = 0.
steps.memory_tip: A critical point is where the derivative is zero. An endpoint is not a critical point, but it still has to be tested.

steps.label: Evaluate f at the critical point and at both endpoints
steps.margin_note: Two marks. BOTH endpoints must appear. Forgetting them is the classic error on this question type, and here it would remove the maximum from the list altogether.
lines: For an absolute extremum on a closed interval, evaluate f at every critical point AND at both endpoints.

recall.must_convey: That f(0) = 0, f(−2) = 4 and f(2) = 4 — the critical point and both endpoints.
accept: evaluate at the critical point and at both endpoints
f of minus two and f of two are both four
rendu endpoints daggara kooda value teesukovali
minus two whole squared is plus four
make a list of the three values

steps.why: An absolute extremum is not the same as a local one. The largest value can sit at an endpoint, where the derivative need not be zero at all, so the endpoints must be in the list.
common_mistakes: Testing only x = 0 and reporting no maximum at all.
Writing f(−2) = −4, by squaring only the 2 and keeping the minus sign.
steps.memory_tip: Square the whole negative number, brackets included: (−2)² = 4, not −4. The bracket is what carries the sign into the square.

steps.label: Compare the values and state both extrema
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. Say that the maximum is reached at BOTH endpoints. An absolute maximum is a single VALUE but it may be attained at more than one point.
lines: The smallest value is 0, reached at the interior point x = 0.
The largest value is 4, and it is reached at BOTH endpoints, x = −2 and x = 2.
So the minimum comes from the critical point and the maximum comes from the endpoints.

lines.text: ∴ absolute minimum = 0 at x = 0,  and absolute maximum = 4 at x = −2 and at x = 2

recall.must_convey: That the absolute minimum is 0 at x = 0 and the absolute maximum is 4, reached at both x = −2 and x = 2.
accept: the absolute minimum is zero at x equal to zero
the maximum happens at both endpoints
minimum is from the critical point and maximum from the ends
compare the three values and pick the largest and smallest

steps.why: The absolute extrema are the largest and smallest members of the list. No second derivative test is needed on a closed interval — comparing the values is the complete method.
common_mistakes: Naming only x = 2 for the maximum and leaving out x = −2.
Giving x = 0 as the minimum value instead of f(0) = 0 as the value.
steps.memory_tip: The maximum VALUE is one number, but the points where it is reached can be several. Report the value first, then every x that gives it.

insider_note: Test both endpoints along with the stationary point. The minimum 0 is interior at x = 0 but the maximum 4 occurs at BOTH ends, which is worth saying.
